title: A Dao that can be spoken
shortSummary: The opening of the Daodejing frames a problem among language, naming and constancy.
curatorialDescription: The passage is not reduced to an anti-language slogan; it is shown with edition, chapter and commentarial context.
researchNote: The Alpha text follows a received edition; excavated variants and Tang commentaries remain to be added.

quote.original: 道可道，非常道；名可名，非常名。
quote.interpretation: The chapter opens with a tension between what can be spoken or named and what is constant.

profile.originalText: 道可道，非常道；名可名，非常名。
profile.punctuatedText: 道可道，非常道；名可名，非常名。
profile.modernZh: 能够说出的道，不是恒常的道；能够命名的名，不是恒常的名。
profile.translationEn: A Dao that can be spoken is not the constant Dao; a name that can be named is not the constant name.
